## Why

Users of `beta` want a greeting on start-up, and the text belongs in `alpha`,
the shared library, so that other tools can use it too.

## Scope

In: the greeting text in `alpha`; printing it in `beta`.

Out: translations; any change to `gamma`.

## Requirements

### R1 Greeting text
`alpha` SHALL provide the greeting `hello, demo` for a caller that asks for it.

#### R1.S1 Default greeting
- GIVEN `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with no name
- THEN it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
  newline)

#### R1.S2 Name too long
- GIVEN a name of 65 characters
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with that name
- THEN it gets an error naming the 64-character limit, and no greeting

### R2 beta prints the greeting
`beta` SHALL print the greeting from `alpha` as its first line of output.

#### R2.S1 Start-up line
- GIVEN `beta` built against `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN `beta` starts with no arguments
- THEN its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of
  start (wall time)

## Approaches

1. Greeting in `alpha`, printed by `beta` (picked: one source of the text).
2. Greeting in `beta` only (rejected: other tools would copy the text).

## Open calls

1. The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points.

One that reviews no single task, such as the whole-change review, counts its own review lines. - A test or lead task: it has reported. 2. **blocked.** Its newest status line, later than its newest dispatch line, is BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT. 3. **dispatched.** A dispatch line names it. A review task is also dispatched once the task it reviews has reported: the lead dispatches a review as soon as it records the report, and writes no dispatch line for it. 4. **ready.** It is not held, and every task in its `after` list is done. 5. **waiting.** Anything else, held tasks included. ### Latest A task's events are the dispatch, status, fix-round, at-base and returned-to-test lines that name it. A review task's events are the review lines of the task it reviews (its own, when it reviews no single task). The newest is the one with the latest UTC, and of those the one written last. The cell is its UTC, a space, and the event in this form: | Event | Cell text after the UTC | |---|---| | dispatch | `dispatch -> (, )` | | status | the status word, then `, ..` and `, unit

/ pass` when the line has them in that form; nothing else | | `T complete`, in words | `DONE` | | review | `review: ` or `review r: `, then `spec ok` or `spec issues`, then `; ` and its counts as ` ` in the order Critical, Important, Minor, joined by `, `, without file and line; `none` when it lists no finding | | fix round | `fix round /5: addressed, open` | | at base | `at base: fail,

pass`, counting the tests the line names | | returned to test | `returned to test: ` | A `|` inside a cell is written `\|`. ## Open findings The ledger's review and fix-round lines give the counts. - **Critical and Important.** For each task that has a review line, take its newest review or fix-round line. A review line gives its Critical and Important counts. A fix-round line gives its ` open` findings, counted as Critical up to the number of Critical findings in the review before it, and the rest as Important. A ruling closes them at any round: when a `Ruling:` line newer than that line begins `Ruling: T open findings`, as in `Ruling: T open findings parked: ; ; `, the task counts 0. A `Ruling:` line in another form closes nothing. Add the counts over all tasks. - **Minor.** The sum of the Minor counts of every review line of the change. Minor findings wait for the whole-change review and the final report's deferred minors, so none closes before integrate. ## Same records, same text - Nothing comes from the wall clock, the session, the node or the space's own commit sha. Every UTC is copied from a record. - Every list follows a fixed order given above: `pod.yaml` order for pins, the spec's order for repos and approvals, byte order for change ids, task order for tasks. - Every empty case has its fixed text: `none`, `none yet`, `-`, `0`. - The records are read as committed (`SKILL.md` section 1.1), and branch heads from the remotes, so the text changes only when a record, a pin or a branch head changes. ## Example A space `proj:demo` with one change, `add-greeting`, in one repo, at a fictional state: ```markdown # Status: proj:demo Generated from the records; never edited by hand.
